message:
fix(update): no release has ever replaced the updater

payloadNames was product_image_names() plus the two data files, and
product_image_names() is the STOP list. A comment defended sharing them: the set
that is stopped and the set that is replaced cannot drift apart. It did not work.
GNLinkUpdater.exe was in neither, so every release since the feature existed has
left the installed updater untouched -- which means a fix to the updater cannot
be delivered by an update, and a manual installer run is required to bootstrap
one.

The two lists answer different questions -- what must not be running while we
replace it, and what we replace -- and exactly one file has different answers.
So product_payload_names() is derived from the stop list rather than equal to it,
and the invariant that matters (stop is a subset of payload) is asserted instead
of assumed. The updater is replaced and not stopped: it runs from a working copy
outside installDir, and validate() compares full destination paths rather than
names, which is what makes that safe.

VerifyDownload now refuses a manifest that does not name everything the swap will
replace. Swap already refused -- but by then the product has been asked to stop
and the user is looking at a closed application, which is exactly what 0.2.109
did. The same answer was available before anything closed.

And the publisher refuses first: gnlink_check_payload_set.py reads the expected
set out of product_payload_names() rather than restating it, and preflight runs
it. Pointed at the manifest that actually broke the field it says "REFUSING: the
manifest does not name GNLinkSetup.exe".

Two tests were passing without checking anything, and the new code exposed both:

  - The post-swap rollback case described an impossible release -- GNLinkSetup.exe
    in payloadNames, absent from the manifest. The same shape as the release that
    shipped. Nothing minded, so it passed.
  - The deploy suite's signature tamper was `sed 's/^0/1/'` and the new signature
    begins with 8, so it edited nothing. That case published a perfectly valid
    release and reported that it had been refused.

Items 1-4 (supervisor-first stop, captured-handle wait, relaunch after the
parent's final exit, SCM path) are not in this commit: their counterexample needs
a real windowed parent and a console child, and RDP is active.
